A: Leans on 'the catalogue's own entry' as authority several times, which weakens the argument if the reader lacks that catalogue
Champagne/brass precious accent is a known AA contrast risk on ivory; flagged for testing but still an added failure point the design does not strictly need
Slight meta-framing verbosity (selection-sentence scaffolding) spends lines on process rather than the design itself
B: Less structural guidance on page-level hierarchy: no fixed positions for critical data, no explicit overview-vs-drill-down density architecture beyond a row-height toggle
Overstates that neumorphism is 'nearly impossible' to retrofit to WCAG 2.2 AA; the directionally right point is asserted beyond what is defensible
No verification/QA step: contrast and semantic-colour discipline are specified but nothing enforces them (A ships explicit QA gates); minor typo 'no gradients fills'
Rejected alternative 3 (playful neobank style) was never a plausible candidate for a private bank, so one of the three rejections does less analytical work

notes: Both converge on the same correct answer (Swiss/International primary with an editorial-serif financial influence) and both nail the fashionable-but-unsuitable rejection with sound contrast and register arguments. A wins on system thinking: derived selection criteria, a two-tier overview/drill-down density architecture, absolute semantic-colour reservation, data-freshness as a regulatory feature, token-level AA guarantees, and shippable QA gates. B is tighter and more concrete in places (named typefaces, hex-class values, 24px targets, focus-ring spec, ARIA live regions, inducement-rule reasoning) but is thinner on composition, enforcement, and picks one strawman rejection. Margin is real but modest; weighted ~4.6 vs ~4.3.
